problem: Semantic navigation for mobile robots in dynamic indoor environments (moved objects, blocked paths) is brittle and hard to explain, and prior maps are not hierarchical or adaptable to navigation goals.
motivation: Real indoor environments change unpredictably, so robots need maps that integrate metric, topological and semantic information and can be updated online. Explainable behavior matters for trust and deployment in industrial, hospital and office settings.
key_idea: Automatically build Hierarchical Semantic Topometric Maps (IntelliMap) from raw data and use them in IntelliNav for global semantic planning into sub-goals, local metric navigation, dynamic replanning, continuous map updates and persistent mission memory.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that combining semantic global planning over a hierarchical map with metric local navigation and persistent memory yields higher success rate, adaptability and legibility than the state of the art in dynamic scenes.
method: IntelliMap: hierarchical mapping framework that automatically generates HSTM (Hierarchical Semantic Topometric Maps) from raw data, integrating metric, topological and semantic layers and adaptable to navigation goals
IntelliNav global planning: builds a path of successive sub-goals from semantic elements of the HSTM up to the final goal
IntelliNav local navigation: reaches each sub-goal using the metric layer of the HSTM
Dynamic replanning: triggered when obstacles persist
Continuous HSTM update and persistent memory: the map is updated at runtime and past mission history is exploited
MultiNav: theoretical distributed multi-robot extension based on synchronized local maps

setting.observation: not specified (raw sensor data, likely RGB-D)
setting.action_space: not specified (sub-goal based global planning with local metric navigation)
setting.simulator: HM3DSem, uHumans2 (simulated realistic multi-room, multi-floor scenes)

results: The abstract reports significant gains in success rate, adaptability and legibility of robot behavior over the state of the art on HM3DSem and uHumans2 dynamic scenes, without giving numbers or naming baselines.
limitations: MultiNav is only a theoretical perspective and is not evaluated
Evaluated only in simulation, with no real-robot results reported in the abstract
